proofs.proof_tex:
First consider any admissible two-sign late-void pair \(\widetilde r^+=g\), \(\widetilde r^-=-g\), where \(g=0\) on \([0,a]\), \(|g(u)|\le M\), and \(g\) is \(L_r\)-Lipschitz. Since \(g(a)=0\), for \(u>a\),
\[
 |g(u)|\le L_r(u-a).
\]
Together with boundedness this yields the pointwise certificate
\[
 |g(u)|\le\min\{L_r(u-a)_+,M\}.
\]
The capped clipped ramp attains equality at every \(u\). Hence
\[
 \left|2\int_0^1g(u)\,du\right|
 \le2\int_0^{1-a}\min\{L_rs,M\}\,ds=d(1-a).
\]

The function \(d(x)\) in the sharp clipped-ramp theorem is continuous and strictly increasing on \([0,1]\), because its derivative is \(2\min\{L_rx,M\}>0\) for \(x>0\). Its endpoint value is
\[
 d(1)=
 \begin{cases}
 L_r,&L_r\le M,\\
 2M-M^2/L_r,&L_r>M,
 \end{cases}
 =d_{\max}.
\]
If \(L_r\le M\), then \(d_{\max}=L_r\le M^2/L_r\), so every \(d<d_{\max}\) lies on the quadratic branch and \(x(d)=\sqrt{d/L_r}\in(0,1)\). If \(L_r>M\), the clipping location \(x=M/L_r\) is interior, its image is \(M^2/L_r\), and direct inversion of the quadratic and affine branches gives the two displayed formulas for \(x(d)\). In every case,
\[
 x(d)\in(0,1),\qquad a(d)=1-x(d)\in(0,1),
 \qquad d(x(d))=d.
\]
This also proves the elbow assertion.

Fix \(d\in(0,d_{\max})\) and select the capped clipped-ramp pair with start \(a_\star=a(d)\). The established membership proposition places this constant-intensity pair in the declared structured class. Define
\[
 \gamma_n=\max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\tau_n^\sigma\notin D_n\}.
\]
Uniform asymptotic honesty therefore implies \(\limsup_n\gamma_n\le\alpha\). The sharp constant-intensity theorem gives
\[
 \Delta_n\ge d(x(d))=d,
 \qquad \eta_n\longrightarrow a(d)^c,
\]
and
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}
 \ge[\eta_n-2\gamma_n]_+.
\]
The event on the left is contained in \(\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}\). Continuity and monotonicity of the positive-part map therefore give
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge[a(d)^c-2\alpha]_+
 =[(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+.
\]

The exact allocation in the sharp clipped-ramp theorem has maximum miscoverage at most \(\alpha\), and its only positive-diameter output is the two-target set of diameter \(\Delta_n\ge d\). Thus, within the selected pair,
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 =[\eta_n-2\alpha]_+
 \longrightarrow[(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+.
\]

To certify optimality within the stated residual late-void method, take any start \(a'=1-x'\) whose limiting causal separation is at least \(d\). The pointwise certificate gives \(d\le d(x')\). Strict monotonicity forces \(x'\ge x(d)\), and hence
\[
 (a')^c=(1-x')^c\le(1-x(d))^c.
\]
This proves the claimed residual-profile envelope without asserting global minimax attainment.

For the required exact diagnostic, specialize to \(c=a_\star=1/2\), \(L_r=1/2\), \(M\ge1/4\), and choose the propensity cap with \(\rho\ge1/2\). The cap qualification is essential. Then
\[
 d(1/2)=1/8,
 \qquad
 [(1/2)^{1/2}-2(0.05)]_+
 =0.6071067811865475\ldots.
\]
Moreover, direct enumeration of the void products gives
\[
 \eta_1=\frac12,
 \qquad \eta_2=\frac34,
 \qquad \eta_3=\frac58,
 \qquad \eta_4=\frac{35}{48}.
\]
Indeed the relevant factor sets are respectively \(\{1\}\), \(\{2\}\), \(\{2,3\}\), and \(\{3,4\}\), with factors \(1-1/(2t)\). If \(\rho<1/2\), already \(\eta_1=1-\rho\), so the four exact values are not asserted there. This diagnostic preserves the \(1/8\) and \(0.60710678\) constants and changes neither the positive calibration theorem nor the separate high-hazard radius result.

The sourced baseline-class lemma records the requirements relevant here. In the constant-intensity clipped-ramp construction,
\[
 e_{nt}(1)=\min\{\rho,c/t\},
 \qquad e_{nt}(0)=1-e_{nt}(1).
\]
These probabilities are deterministic functions of every history, strictly between zero and one, and sum to one. The established membership proposition supplies fixed bounded potential outcomes and predictable zero regression. Thus every such array lies in Li and Zhao's baseline binary adaptive class.

We verify failure of the negligible-increment condition. Put
\[
 g(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a_\star)_+,M\},
 \qquad
 X_{nt}=(A_{nt}-e_{nt})\frac{\sigma g(t/n)}{e_{nt}}.
\]
Predictable randomization yields
\[
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})
 =g(t/n)^2\{e_{nt}^{-1}-1\}.
\]
Distinct increments are orthogonal by iterated conditioning. Once \(n\) is large, the cap is inactive whenever \(g(t/n)>0\). Therefore, if \(W_n\) is the variance of the \(\sqrt n\)-scaled scalar AIPW error,
\[
 W_n=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^ng(t/n)^2(t/c-1),
 \qquad
 \frac{W_n}{n}\longrightarrow
 w_\star:=\frac1c\int_{a_\star}^1u g(u)^2\,du>0.
\]
At \(t=n\), the outcome envelope is at least \(g(1)>0\), the regression envelope is zero, and the smaller binary assignment probability is \(c/n\) for large \(n\). Hence the scalar negligible-maximum ratio from the sourced Condition 3(ii) satisfies
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 W_n^{-1}n^{-1}
 \max_{1\le t\le n}\frac{(L_t+M_t)^2}{\underline e_t^2}
 \ge\frac{g(1)^2}{c^2w_\star}>0.
\]
It cannot be \(o(1)\), proving the stated failure. At the unprojected two-arm level, the identically zero control contribution also produces a zero control row and column, consistent with the same Gaussian obstruction.

Now let the confidence sets be uniformly asymptotically honest over Li and Zhao's baseline class. The inclusion just proved gives, for the selected constant-intensity pair,
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\gamma_n\le\alpha.
\]
We do not invoke the structured-class premise of the optimized theorem. Instead, use directly the constant-pair finite common-subprobability inequality:
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}
 \ge[\eta_n-2\gamma_n]_+.
\]
At start \(a(d)=1-x(d)\), the sharp theorem gives \(\Delta_n\ge d\) and \(\eta_n\to a(d)^c\). Therefore
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge[(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+.
\]
This direct argument constructs no procedure over the baseline class and consequently transfers neither the pair-specific attaining rule nor the positive profile-net calibration theorem.

added_lemmas.statement:
Every member of the intensity-optimized clipped-ramp family has fixed potential outcomes bounded by \(M\), valid predictable probabilities \(0<e_{nt}\le\rho<1\), and predictable zero regressions. Its profiles satisfy
\[
 q_\star\in\mathcal Q,\qquad r^\sigma\in\mathcal R,
 \qquad r_{nt}(1)=r^\sigma(t/n).
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), the propensity cap is inactive at every \(t\ge\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil\) and at every \(t>\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor\); the two profile discrepancies defining \(G_n\) are zero, the early rare-arm term and its predictable quadratic variation are zero, and hence \(G_n=\Omega\). This is only an eventual assertion: the family is not asserted to satisfy the all-\(n\) profile contract or to belong to the full declared structured class for every \(n\).

Moreover, for every \(q'\in\mathcal Q\) and \(u\in[0,1]\),
\[
 q'(u)\ge q_\star(u).
\]
Consequently, for every fixed start \(a_\star\), every \(n\), and every deterministic design of the form \(e_{nt}^{q'}=\min\{\rho,q'(t/n)/t\}\),
\[
 \prod_{t=\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor+1}^{n}(1-e_{nt}^{q'})
 \le
 \prod_{t=\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor+1}^{n}
 \left[1-\min\{\rho,q_\star(t/n)/t\}\right].
\]
Thus \(q_\star\) pointwise maximizes the common late-void mass within this deterministic intensity-profile design family.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The potential outcomes and regressions in the construction are deterministic, hence fixed under randomization and predictable, respectively. Since
\[
 0\le g_{a_\star}(u)\le M,
\]
both potential-outcome arms are bounded in absolute value by \(M\). Also \(q_\star(u)\ge c/2>0\), so
\[
 0<e_{nt}=\min\{\rho,q_\star(t/n)/t\}\le\rho<1.
\]
The displayed sequential law then gives the declared predictable binary randomization, and the two arm probabilities \(e_{nt}\) and \(1-e_{nt}\) sum to one.

We next verify the intensity conditions. Directly,
\[
 q_\star(0)=\max\{c,c/2\}=c,
 \qquad c/2\le q_\star(u)\le c\le K.
\]
The affine map \(u\mapsto c-L_qu\) is \(L_q\)-Lipschitz, and the scalar map \(x\mapsto\max\{x,c/2\}\) is nondecreasing and one-Lipschitz. Therefore
\[
 |q_\star(u)-q_\star(v)|\le L_q|u-v|,
\]
so \(q_\star\in\mathcal Q\). Likewise, \(|r^\sigma(u)|=g_{a_\star}(u)\le M\le B\), because \(B=M+M_m\) and \(M_m\ge0\). Both maps \(u\mapsto(u-a_\star)_+\) and \(x\mapsto\min\{x,M\}\) are one-Lipschitz on their respective domains. Hence
\[
 |r^\sigma(u)-r^\sigma(v)|\le L_r|u-v|,
\]
and \(r^\sigma\in\mathcal R\). Since the regression is zero, the finite residual is exactly
\[
 r_{nt}(1)=Y_{nt}^\sigma(1)-m_{nt}(1)=r^\sigma(t/n).
\]

Because \(q_\star\le c\), the cap is inactive whenever \(t\ge c/\rho\). The primitive cutoff conditions give
\[
 n\varepsilon_n\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad a_\star n\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Thus, for all sufficiently large \(n\), both \(t\ge\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil\) and \(t>\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor\) imply \(t\ge c/\rho\), and then
\[
 t e_{nt}=q_\star(t/n).
\]
The intensity discrepancy in \(G_n\) is therefore zero, and the residual discrepancy was already shown to be zero. Since \(\varepsilon_n+n^{-1}\to0<a_\star\), eventually
\[
 t<\lceil n\varepsilon_n\rceil
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 t/n<\varepsilon_n+n^{-1}<a_\star.
\]
For every such \(t\), \(r_{nt}(1)=0\). Every summand of the early rare-arm martingale and of its predictable quadratic variation is consequently zero. All three clauses in the definition of \(G_n\) hold surely, proving \(G_n=\Omega\) eventually. At a finite included index where \(q_\star(t/n)/t>\rho\), however, the intensity discrepancy equals \(q_\star(t/n)-t\rho\), which need not be bounded by \(\delta_{q,n}\). This proves precisely why the conclusion is eventual and does not establish the all-\(n\) profile contract.

Finally, take any \(q'\in\mathcal Q\). The anchor and Lipschitz conditions give
\[
 q'(u)\ge q'(0)-L_qu=c-L_qu,
\]
while the intensity floor gives \(q'(u)\ge c/2\). Hence
\[
 q'(u)\ge\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}=q_\star(u).
\]
The function \(x\mapsto\min\{\rho,x/t\}\) is nondecreasing, so \(e_{nt}^{q'}\ge e_{nt}^{q_\star}\), and therefore \(1-e_{nt}^{q'}\le1-e_{nt}^{q_\star}\). Every factor is nonnegative. Multiplication over the late indices proves the displayed product inequality and the claimed finite-sample pointwise optimality.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix a member of the intensity-optimized clipped-ramp family and define
\[
 m_n=\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor,
 \qquad V_n=\bigcap_{t=m_n+1}^{n}\{A_{nt}=0\},
 \qquad
 \eta_n^\star=\prod_{t=m_n+1}^{n}
 \left[1-\min\{\rho,q_\star(t/n)/t\}\right],
\]
and
\[
 \Delta_n=\tau_n^+-\tau_n^-
 =\frac2n\sum_{t=1}^{n}\min\{L_r(t/n-a_\star)_+,M\}.
\]
For any possibly randomized complete-log confidence set \(D_n=D_n(O_n,U)\), where \(U\) is independent of the experiment and identically distributed under the two signs, put
\[
 \gamma_n=\max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\tau_n^\sigma\notin D_n\}.
\]
With \([z]_+=\max\{z,0\}\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(\varnothing)=0\), for every \(n\) and each sign,
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}
 \ge[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+.
\]
For every \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), this inequality is attained within this two-sign subexperiment by a possibly randomized complete-log confidence set with maximum miscoverage at most \(\alpha\) and, under either sign,
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}
 =[\eta_n^\star-2\alpha]_+.
\]
Writing \(x=1-a_\star\), one has \(\Delta_n\ge d(x)\) for every \(n\) and \(\Delta_n\to d(x)\), where
\[
 d(x)=2\int_0^x\min\{L_rs,M\}\,ds
 =\begin{cases}
 L_rx^2,&L_rx\le M,\\
 2Mx-M^2/L_r,&L_rx>M.
 \end{cases}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \eta_n^\star\longrightarrow\omega(a_\star)=\exp\{-H(a_\star)\},
 \qquad H(a)=\int_a^1\frac{q_\star(u)}u\,du.
\]
If \(0\le L_q\le c/2\), then
\[
 H(a)=c\log(1/a)-L_q(1-a).
\]
If \(L_q>c/2\) and \(u_q=c/(2L_q)\), then
\[
 H(a)=
 \begin{cases}
 (c/2)\log(1/a),&a\ge u_q,\\
 c\log(u_q/a)-L_q(u_q-a)+(c/2)\log(1/u_q),&a<u_q.
 \end{cases}
\]
The attainment assertion is confined to the displayed two-sign subexperiment.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The causal targets follow directly from the fixed potential outcomes:
\[
 \tau_n^\sigma=\frac{\sigma}{n}\sum_{t=1}^n g_{a_\star}(t/n),
 \qquad
 \Delta_n=\frac2n\sum_{t=1}^n g_{a_\star}(t/n)>0.
\]
The function \(u\mapsto g_{a_\star}(u)\) is nondecreasing. On each interval \(((t-1)/n,t/n]\), its value is at most \(g_{a_\star}(t/n)\), so the right Riemann sum satisfies
\[
 \Delta_n\ge2\int_0^1g_{a_\star}(u)\,du=d(1-a_\star).
\]
The function is continuous, hence its right Riemann sums converge to the same integral. Substitution \(s=u-a_\star\) and direct integration before and after the clipping point \(s=M/L_r\) give the two displayed formulas for \(d(x)\).

Let \(V_{n,s}=\bigcap_{t=m_n+1}^{s}\{A_{nt}=0\}\), with \(V_{n,m_n}=\Omega\). The event \(V_{n,s-1}\) is \(\mathcal F_{n,s-1}\)-measurable. Predictable randomization and the deterministic propensity in the family give, under either sign,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \Pr_\sigma(V_{n,s})
 &=\mathbb E_\sigma\!\left[
 \mathbf1_{V_{n,s-1}}
 \Pr_\sigma(A_{ns}=0\mid\mathcal F_{n,s-1})
 \right]\\
 &=\left[1-\min\{\rho,q_\star(s/n)/s\}\right]
 \Pr_\sigma(V_{n,s-1}).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Iteration proves \(\Pr_\sigma(V_n)=\eta_n^\star\).

On \(V_n\), every observed outcome is zero under both signs. Indeed, for \(t\le m_n\), one has \(t/n\le a_\star\), hence both treated outcomes are zero; for \(t>m_n\), the void event forces the control arm, whose potential outcome is zero. The propensity and regression logs are also identical under the two signs. Since the assignment probabilities are the same deterministic numbers under both signs, repeated conditioning shows that the restrictions of the two laws of \((O_n,U)\) to \(V_n\) coincide. Denote this common subprobability measure by \(\nu_n\); it has mass \(\eta_n^\star\) and is dominated by each full law.

For \(E_{\sigma,n}=\{\tau_n^\sigma\in D_n\}\), domination and the definition of \(\gamma_n\) imply
\[
 \nu_n(E_{\sigma,n}^c)\le\gamma_n.
\]
The union bound under \(\nu_n\) gives
\[
 \nu_n(E_{+,n}\cap E_{-,n})\ge\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n.
\]
On this intersection the same set contains two points separated by \(\Delta_n\). Domination by either sign-specific law and nonnegativity yield
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}
 \ge[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+.
\]

For attainment, take an independent uniform random variable \(U\). On \(V_n^c\), the first treated time after \(m_n\) has a nonzero observed outcome whose sign identifies \(\sigma\); report the corresponding true singleton. On \(V_n\), if \(\eta_n^\star>2\alpha\), assign conditional probabilities
\[
 \frac{\alpha}{\eta_n^\star},\qquad
 \frac{\alpha}{\eta_n^\star},\qquad
 1-\frac{2\alpha}{\eta_n^\star}
\]
to the positive singleton, the negative singleton, and the two-target set. If \(\alpha<\eta_n^\star\le2\alpha\), assign conditional probabilities
\[
 \frac{\eta_n^\star-\alpha}{\eta_n^\star},\qquad
 \frac{\eta_n^\star-\alpha}{\eta_n^\star},\qquad
 \frac{2\alpha-\eta_n^\star}{\eta_n^\star}
\]
to the two singletons and the empty set. If \(\eta_n^\star\le\alpha\), report the empty set on \(V_n\). In each case the displayed probabilities are nonnegative and sum to one. Direct accounting gives miscoverage at most \(\alpha\) under each sign, while the two-target set is selected with unconditional probability exactly \([\eta_n^\star-2\alpha]_+\). This proves finite-sample sharpness inside the pair.

It remains to compute the void limit. Because \(m_n/n\to a_\star>0\) and \(q_\star\le c\), the cap is inactive throughout \(t>m_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Put \(p_{nt}=q_\star(t/n)/t\). Then \(\max_{t>m_n}p_{nt}\to0\), and the elementary identity
\[
 0\le-\log(1-y)-y=\int_0^y\frac{x}{1-x}\,dx
 \le\frac{y^2}{2(1-y)},\qquad 0\le y<1,
\]
implies
\[
 \left|\log\eta_n^\star+\sum_{t=m_n+1}^np_{nt}\right|
 \le
 \frac{1}{2\{1-\max_{t>m_n}p_{nt}\}}
 \sum_{t=m_n+1}^np_{nt}^2.
\]
The right-hand side tends to zero because
\[
 \sum_{t=m_n+1}^np_{nt}^2
 \le c^2\sum_{t=m_n+1}^nt^{-2}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Furthermore,
\[
 \sum_{t=m_n+1}^np_{nt}
 =\frac1n\sum_{t=m_n+1}^n
 \frac{q_\star(t/n)}{t/n}
 \longrightarrow\int_{a_\star}^1\frac{q_\star(u)}u\,du=H(a_\star),
\]
by right-Riemann convergence on the compact interval bounded away from zero. Hence \(\eta_n^\star\to\exp\{-H(a_\star)\}\).

If \(0\le L_q\le c/2\), then \(c-L_qu\ge c/2\) for all \(u\in[0,1]\), so
\[
 H(a)=\int_a^1\left(\frac cu-L_q\right)du
 =c\log(1/a)-L_q(1-a).
\]
If \(L_q>c/2\), the two pieces meet at \(u_q=c/(2L_q)\in(0,1)\). For \(a\ge u_q\), the profile equals \(c/2\) throughout \([a,1]\), giving \((c/2)\log(1/a)\). For \(a<u_q\), splitting the integral at \(u_q\) gives
\[
 \int_a^{u_q}\left(\frac cu-L_q\right)du
 +\int_{u_q}^1\frac{c}{2u}\,du
 =c\log(u_q/a)-L_q(u_q-a)+(c/2)\log(1/u_q),
\]
as asserted.

added_lemmas.statement:
Assume \(L_r>0\), and define
\[
 d_{\max}=\begin{cases}
 L_r,&L_r\le M,\\
 2M-M^2/L_r,&L_r>M.
 \end{cases}
\]
For \(0<d<d_{\max}\), let
\[
 x(d)=\begin{cases}
 \sqrt{d/L_r},&d\le M^2/L_r,\\
 \{d+M^2/L_r\}/(2M),&d>M^2/L_r,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad a(d)=1-x(d).
\]
Select the intensity-optimized clipped-ramp pair with start \(a(d)\), and write
\[
 \gamma_n=\max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\tau_n^\sigma\notin D_n\}.
\]
If this selected pair satisfies \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\gamma_n\le\alpha\), then, under each sign,
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge
 \left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+.
\]
This envelope is jointly optimal among deterministic late-void two-sign witnesses of the stated form with intensity profile in \(\mathcal Q\), residual magnitude bounded by \(M\), and residual Lipschitz modulus at most \(L_r\). For each selected two-sign pair, the exact randomized allocation attains the displayed asymptotic bound, but no globally attaining procedure over the full structured class is asserted.

The residual clipping elbow is \(d_r=M^2/L_r\) and is interior precisely when \(L_r>M\). If \(L_q>c/2\), the intensity profile has the additional elbow
\[
 d_q=d\!\left(1-\frac{c}{2L_q}\right).
\]
When both elbows are interior, either strict ordering \(d_q<d_r\) or \(d_r<d_q\) is possible under the declared parameter restrictions.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The constant-intensity optimized theorem proves that \(d(x)\) is continuous and strictly increasing on \([0,1]\), has endpoint value \(d_{\max}\), and satisfies
\[
 d(x(d))=d,qquad x(d)\in(0,1),qquad a(d)=1-x(d)\in(0,1).
\]
Fix \(d\) and the stated intensity-optimized pair. Its sharp finite-sample theorem gives
\[
 \Delta_n\ge d(x(d))=d,
 \qquad
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}
 \ge[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+,
\]
and
\[
 \eta_n^\star\longrightarrow
 \exp\{-H(a(d))\}=\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}.
\]
The event at threshold \(\Delta_n\) is contained in the event at threshold \(d\). Since the positive-part map is continuous and nondecreasing, the premise \(\limsup_n\gamma_n\le\alpha\) yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \liminf_n\Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 &\ge\liminf_n[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+\\
 &\ge\left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+.
 \end{aligned}
\]

For the optimization certificate, consider any two-sign late-void residual \(\widetilde r^+=g\), \(\widetilde r^-=-g\) that vanishes on \([0,a']\), is bounded in magnitude by \(M\), and is \(L_r\)-Lipschitz. Since \(g(a')=0\),
\[
 |g(u)|\le\min\{L_r(u-a')_+,M\}.
\]
Thus its limiting causal separation is at most \(d(1-a')\). To attain separation at least \(d\), strict monotonicity forces
\[
 1-a'\ge x(d),\qquad a'\le a(d).
\]
For any \(q'\in\mathcal Q\), the intensity-properties proposition gives \(q'(u)\ge q_\star(u)\) and hence a finite late-void product no larger than the \(q_\star\) product at the same start. Under \(q_\star\), the limiting void mass at start \(a'\) is \(\exp\{-H(a')\}\). Because the integrand \(q_\star(u)/u\) is positive and \(a'\le a(d)\),
\[
 H(a')\ge H(a(d)),
 \qquad
 \exp\{-H(a')\}\le\exp\{-H(a(d))\}.
\]
The clipped residual at \(a(d)\) and the pointwise-minimal intensity \(q_\star\) attain equality in both comparisons. This is the announced joint late-void optimality certificate.

The exact randomized allocation in the sharp theorem has maximum miscoverage at most \(\alpha\) for every \(n\), and its only positive-diameter output is the two-target set, whose diameter \(\Delta_n\) is at least \(d\). Hence
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 =[\eta_n^\star-2\alpha]_+
 \longrightarrow
 \left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+.
\]
This rule uses knowledge of the selected pair and therefore proves pairwise, not global, attainment.

The residual calculation gives its interior kink at \(x_r=M/L_r\), whose image is \(d_r=M^2/L_r\); one has \(x_r\in(0,1)\) exactly when \(L_r>M\). When \(L_q>c/2\), the intensity kink is at \(u_q=c/(2L_q)\), hence at \(x_q=1-u_q\) on the diameter scale and at \(d_q=d(x_q)\). If both kinks are interior, then \(x_r\in(0,1)\), while as \(L_q\) ranges over \((c/2,\infty)\), \(x_q=1-c/(2L_q)\) ranges over \((0,1)\). Choosing \(x_q<x_r\) or \(x_q>x_r\), and using strict monotonicity of \(d\), gives respectively \(d_q<d_r\) or \(d_q>d_r\). Thus no ordering is forced by the primitive restrictions.

added_lemmas.statement:
Every intensity-optimized clipped-ramp array belongs, for every \(n\), to Li and Zhao's baseline binary finite-population adaptive-design class, and its nonzero late rare-arm increments violate their negligible-increment Condition 3(ii). Consequently, if a sequence of possibly randomized complete-log confidence sets is asymptotically \((1-\alpha)\)-honest uniformly over that baseline class, then for every \(0<d<d_{\max}\), under each sign of the intensity-optimized clipped-ramp pair with start \(a(d)=1-x(d)\),
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge
 \left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+.
\]
This transfers only the converse. It transfers neither the pair-specific attaining rule nor the positive profile-net calibration theorem.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For every \(n,t\), the two assignment probabilities are
\[
 e_{nt}(1)=\min\{\rho,q_\star(t/n)/t\},
 \qquad e_{nt}(0)=1-e_{nt}(1).
\]
They are deterministic functions of every available history, strictly between zero and one, and sum to one. The intensity-properties proposition proves that the potential outcomes are fixed and bounded and that the zero regression is predictable. These are exactly the relevant binary baseline requirements recorded in the sourced Li--Zhao class lemma. This every-\(n\) baseline inclusion does not use the profile-contract event.

We verify the negligible-increment obstruction directly. Fix a start \(a_\star\) and write
\[
 g(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a_\star)_+,M\},
 \qquad
 X_{nt}=(A_{nt}-e_{nt})\frac{\sigma g(t/n)}{e_{nt}}.
\]
Predictable randomization gives
\[
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_\sigma(X_{nt}^2\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})
 =g(t/n)^2\{e_{nt}^{-1}-1\}.
\]
Distinct martingale increments are orthogonal by iterated conditioning. For all sufficiently large \(n\), the cap is inactive at every \(t>\lfloor a_\star n\rfloor\). Therefore the variance \(W_n\) of the \(\sqrt n\)-scaled scalar AIPW error is
\[
 W_n=\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n
 g(t/n)^2\left\{\frac{t}{q_\star(t/n)}-1\right\}.
\]
Since \(q_\star\ge c/2\) and \(g\) is continuous,
\[
 \frac{W_n}{n}\longrightarrow
 w_\star:=\int_{a_\star}^1
 \frac{u g(u)^2}{q_\star(u)}\,du>0.
\]
At \(t=n\), \(g(1)>0\), the regression envelope is zero, and, for large \(n\), the smaller binary assignment probability is \(q_\star(1)/n\). Thus the scalar negligible-maximum ratio in Condition 3(ii) obeys
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 W_n^{-1}n^{-1}
 \max_{1\le t\le n}\frac{(L_t+M_t)^2}{\underline e_t^2}
 \ge
 \lim_{n\to\infty}
 \frac{g(1)^2 n}{q_\star(1)^2W_n}
 =\frac{g(1)^2}{q_\star(1)^2w_\star}>0.
\]
It is not \(o(1)\), proving failure of the cited Gaussian premise rather than assuming a limit law.

Now suppose the confidence sets are uniformly asymptotically honest over the Li--Zhao baseline class. The every-\(n\) inclusion just proved implies, for the selected two-sign pair,
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\gamma_n\le\alpha.
\]
Use directly the finite common-subprobability inequality from the sharp intensity-optimized theorem:
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}
 \ge[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+.
\]
For the start \(a(d)=1-x(d)\), the same theorem gives \(\Delta_n\ge d\) and
\(\eta_n^\star\to\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}\). Event inclusion, continuity of the positive part, and the last bound on \(\gamma_n\) yield the displayed converse. No procedure on the baseline class has been constructed, so neither pairwise attainment nor positive structured-class calibration transfers.

proposed.name: Intensity-optimized clipped-ramp family
proposed.construction:
Fix \(c>0\), \(\rho\in(0,1)\), \(a_\star\in(0,1)\), \(M>0\), \(L_r>0\), \(K\ge c\), and \(L_q\ge0\). Define
\[
 q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\},\qquad
 g_{a_\star}(u)=\min\{L_r(u-a_\star)_+,M\}.
\]
For \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\), put
\[
 \bar q^\sigma=q_\star,\qquad r^\sigma(u)=\sigma g_{a_\star}(u),\qquad
 e_{nt}=\min\{\rho,q_\star(t/n)/t\},
\]
and set \(m_{nt}(0)=m_{nt}(1)=0\), \(Y_{nt}^\sigma(0)=0\), and \(Y_{nt}^\sigma(1)=r^\sigma(t/n)\). The sequential randomization law is
\(\Pr_\sigma(A_{nt}=1\mid\mathcal F_{n,t-1})=e_{nt}\), and the complete observation is \(O_n=(A_{n1:n},e_{n1:n},Y_{n1:n}^{\mathrm{obs}},m_{n1:n})\).

prose_updates.tldr: At the critical rare-arm boundary, the finite-population AIPW error need not be Gaussian. On this note's original structured binary profile subclass, a stopped adaptive-to-Bernoulli-to-Poisson transfer and directed-rational convolution give a computable atom-safe interval with uniform randomization coverage and explicit oracle slack. Separately, the retained constant-intensity clipped-ramp theorem optimizes the residual late-void obstruction under structured-class honesty. A distinct pointwise-minimal intensity \(q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}\) yields the jointly optimized pair-honesty envelope \(\left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+\), with residual and intensity elbows that may occur in either order. Direct every-\(n\) inclusion transfers only this converse to Li and Zhao's baseline adaptive class. Exact attainment is pairwise only. The exact \(1/8\), \(0.60710678\), directed \(13/32\), and high-hazard \(0.442M\) results remain unchanged.

project_justification.gap: Li and Zhao's baseline adaptive-design class permits positive history-dependent assignment probabilities, but their Gaussian AIPW theorem requires a negligible-maximum condition that fails at bounded cumulative hazard. Existing adaptive and i.i.d. width results neither calibrate the signed atomic compound-Poisson law nor jointly optimize the complete-log common-void obstruction over the declared intensity, outcome-bound, and residual-Lipschitz restrictions.
project_justification.niche: The boundary has distinct positive and converse deliverables. Structured deterministic profiles support computable atom-safe calibration. For information limits, the retained constant-intensity clipped ramp optimizes residual separation, while the separate profile \(q_\star(u)=\max\{c-L_qu,c/2\}\) is pointwise minimal in \(\mathcal Q\) and therefore maximizes late-void mass for each fixed start. Combining the two yields a pair-honesty frontier with both intensity and residual elbows.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies the finite adaptive-to-Poisson transfer and profile-net interval theorem on the original structured subclass, the retained exact constant-intensity clipped-ramp tradeoff, and a separate exact intensity-optimized two-sign tradeoff. The new joint envelope is proved under honesty for the selected pair because the new family's profile event is guaranteed only eventually, not for every \(n\). A direct baseline-class inclusion argument transfers only the converse to Li and Zhao's class; pairwise attainment and positive calibration retain their separate scopes.

prose_updates.related_work: Li and Zhao (2026) provide the closest design-based setup: fixed finite-population potential outcomes, positive assignment probabilities that may be prespecified functions of history, and predictable AIPW regression. Their baseline binary class contains both the retained constant-intensity clipped ramps and the separate intensity-optimized arrays for every \(n\), but their Theorem 4(ii) assumes Condition 3; both bounded-hazard witnesses fail its negligible-maximum part because late standardized increments remain nonnegligible. The constant-intensity structured-class converse and the direct baseline-class joint-intensity converse are therefore logically separate. Only converse bounds transfer; matching confidence-set constructions remain sharp inside selected two-sign experiments, and the positive profile-net theorem remains confined to this note's original structured subclass. Bibaut and Kallus (2025) organize adaptive inference into Gaussian repair, always-valid methods, and direct inversion of nonnormal laws. Waudby-Smith et al. (2024), Freidling, Zhao, and Gao (2026), and Cho, Bibaut, and Kallus (2025) do not supply the present finite-population signed atomic calibration or jointly optimized common-void envelope. Chen et al. (2026) obtain a compound-Poisson HT law under independent Poisson importance sampling, while Hong, Leung, and Li (2020) treat limited overlap with diverging effective information. Shekhar and Ramdas (2023) prove i.i.d. bounded-mean width bounds. Barbour and Xia (1999) support compound-Poisson error accounting, and Bhattacharjee and Goldstein (2019) identify the generalized Dickman constant-profile reduction. Liberali et al. (2025) remain the applied consumer, conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint bridge for GUSTO-1 and EUROPA.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The finite-transfer theorem couples the AIPW statistic, not the complete experiments, and therefore does not imply the all-estimator lower bounds. Those bounds instead use exact common subprobabilities on late-arm void events. The retained constant-intensity theorem has its original structured-class premise. For the separate intensity-optimized family, \(G_n=\Omega\) is proved only eventually: at a finite included index where \(q_\star(t/n)/t>\rho\), the intensity discrepancy can exceed \(\delta_{q,n}\). Its joint frontier therefore assumes honesty on the selected pair rather than all-\(n\) membership in the structured class. Both matching procedures know their selected pair, so neither establishes global minimax attainment. Li--Zhao inclusion transfers only converse bounds. The positive theorem still requires its supplied profile and early-variation contracts, and the \(0.442M\) high-hazard result remains a subfamily upper bound. The polynomial bit-complexity question remains open because no polynomial bound controls profile boxes straddling the certification boundary.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Uniform finite-experiment coverage applies to the original bounded Lipschitz intensity and signed-residual profile subclass with its supplied common profile event, early quadratic-variation envelope, and certified inputs. The constant-intensity envelope \([(1-x(d))^c-2\alpha]_+\) retains its structured-class honesty premise. The stronger joint-intensity envelope \(\left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+\) is a pair-honesty conclusion for the separate \(q_\star\) experiment, whose profile contract is only eventually exact. Direct every-\(n\) baseline inclusion transfers that joint converse, but neither positive calibration nor attainment, to Li and Zhao's class. Exact attainment is confined to each selected two-sign pair; no global minimax procedure is claimed. The original linear-ramp frontier, exact \(1/8\) and \(0.60710678\) diagnostic with its \(\rho\ge1/2\) cap qualification, directed \(13/32\) certificate, and high-hazard \(0.442M\) radius remain valid. No polynomial certificate-complexity exponent is asserted. The Liberali et al. application remains conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint bridge.
